title: Stay Organized Across Multiple Application Systems
summary: Learn how IB students can manage Common App, UCAS, OUAC, university portals, documents, essays, and deadlines from September through November.
body_markdown:
Applying to universities in several countries can mean managing Common App, UCAS, OUAC, direct applications, scholarships, and university portals simultaneously. To **stay organized across multiple application systems** , use one external master tracker rather than relying on separate platform dashboards.


This matters during the September-to-November IB term, when coursework, predicted grades, references, admissions tests, and early deadlines often overlap. An effective system gives every requirement a deadline, owner, status, and official source.


### Why multiple application systems become confusing


Application platforms organize information differently. Common App separates general information from college-specific requirements, UCAS connects course choices with a school reference, and OUAC applications may lead to additional university portals.


Submitting the central form may be only one stage. Universities can require supplementary forms, portfolios, test scores, financial aid documents, or account activation afterward. No single platform reliably displays tasks located elsewhere.


IB students also coordinate materials controlled by different people. Counselors may submit transcripts, predicted grades, references, and school reports, but students remain responsible for checking what each institution requires.


### Build one master application tracker


Create a spreadsheet with **one row per university or course choice** , not one row per platform. Two universities using Common App may have different essays, testing policies, and deadlines.


Field What to record


University and course Institution, campus, major, or UCAS course code


Application system Common App, UCAS, OUAC, or direct portal


Admission plan Early Decision, Early Action, regular, rolling, or equal consideration


Official deadline Date, time, and time zone from the official source


Internal deadlines School deadline and personal target date


Student tasks Essays, forms, payment, tests, and portfolio


School tasks Transcript, predictions, reference, and school report


Additional forms Scholarships, financial aid, residence, or departmental forms


Status Not started, drafting, requested, ready, submitted, or received


Verification Official link and date last checked


Add notes for word limits, interviews, and score-reporting rules. The tracker is your planning **source of truth** , while official platforms remain the places where information is submitted.


### Separate deadlines into four layers


A university can have several relevant deadlines. Tracking only the final submission date creates unnecessary risk.


### Official application deadline


Use the date published by the university or application service. For 2027 UK entry, UCAS lists **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** for Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, and veterinary medicine or science courses. The equal-consideration deadline for most other undergraduate courses is **13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time** .


Common App institutions set their own deadlines. Common App explains that applications are generally due by **11:59 p.m. in the applicant's local time zone** on the displayed date, but applicants should verify each college's instructions.


### School deadline


Schools often require materials earlier so counselors can check qualifications, add predicted grades, prepare references, and submit documents. For UCAS, the application cannot be sent without its reference, making the school's internal date operationally important.


Ask for the school calendar in September. Record separate dates for requesting references, confirming predictions, reviewing forms, and authorizing submission.


### Personal target date


Set a target **7-14 days before** the applicable school or official deadline. This buffer allows time for payment failures, portal errors, missing documents, and final corrections. It should be used for checking, not first drafting.


### Follow-up deadline


After submission, universities may issue new dates for supplementary applications, financial documents, interviews, or applicant-portal tasks. Transfer each date from the email or portal into your calendar immediately.


### Follow a September-to-November plan


### September: map the process


Finalize your university list, identify every platform, and enter all known requirements into the tracker. Verify information on official university or course pages rather than general deadline summaries.


Request references and confirm how your school sends **IB transcripts and predicted grades** . Predictions are not achieved results and should never be entered as final examination scores. The[RevisionDojo guide to IB predicted grade submission](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-are-ib-predicted-grades-submitted-to-universities-what-every-student-needs-to-know) explains this distinction.


Prepare reusable source documents:


- A complete activities and awards inventory
- An accurate list of IB subjects marked **HL** or **SL**
- School, address, identity, and qualification details
- A folder for transcripts, scores, portfolios, and receipts
- A list of essay prompts, limits, and destinations


### October: prioritize dependent tasks


Complete October applications first. Next, address work involving other people, including references, transcript requests, predicted-grade confirmation, and portfolio review.


Do not submit identical writing without checking each prompt. UCAS responses, a Common App essay, and academic supplements assess different evidence. Maintain a bank of experiences, then adapt material honestly and precisely.


The[global IB university application guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-apply-to-university-as-an-ib-student-step-by-step-guide-for-global-admissions) helps compare national procedures. US applicants can consult the[IB guide to US college applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-in-college-apps-us) for accurate reporting of subjects, transcripts, and predictions.


### November: submit and verify


Many US early plans have November deadlines, although dates vary. The[Common App first-year guide](https://www.commonapp.org/apply/first-year-students/) confirms that institutions determine their own writing, testing, and recommendation requirements.


Before submitting, compare the preview with your passport and school records. Check your legal name, birth date, course levels, grades, admission plan, intended major, essay attachment, and payment.


Save the confirmation and a PDF copy where available. Mark the application **submitted** , but not complete until the institution confirms receipt of all required materials.


### Organize files, accounts, and responsibilities


Use folders for the master tracker, each application system, financial aid, and submission confirmations. Label drafts consistently, such as` University_Course_Draft03_2026-10-12` , and keep only the current version in a` FINAL-CHECK` folder.


Use a password manager and multi-factor authentication where offered. Keep passwords out of shared spreadsheets, use a regularly checked personal email address, and filter messages containing phrases such as “action required” or “application received.”


Assign every tracker task to the **student** , **counselor** , **teacher** , **parent or guardian** , or **testing agency** . Work handled by someone else should be marked **requested** , not complete. Record the request date, follow-up date, and confirmation of receipt.


### Protect your IB workload


Use two fixed application sessions weekly, one for writing and one for administration. Preserve separate study periods for IB revision, assessments, and coursework.


During a short weekly review:


1. Sort the tracker by the earliest internal deadline.
2. Choose one writing and one administrative priority.
3. Follow up on requested materials.
4. Check submitted-application portals once.
5. Schedule IB study before optional application work.


The[RevisionDojo plan for balancing IB and university applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-do-i-help-my-teen-balance-ib-and-university-applications) provides a practical two-lane structure.


### Common mistakes to avoid


- Tracking application deadlines but missing scholarships, tests, or portfolios
- Assuming **submitted** means every document has been received
- Using unofficial summaries instead of checking primary sources
- Ignoring time zones or school-specific internal deadlines
- Entering predicted grades as achieved results
- Reusing essays without checking the prompt and word limit
- Checking portals constantly instead of following a schedule


### Conclusion


To stay organized across multiple application systems, centralize planning while treating official portals as authoritative. Track each university separately, distinguish official and internal deadlines, assign ownership, and verify receipt after submission.
